title: GPU hotpath contingency sizing grid
body:
Purpose:
This working worksheet defines a minimal "hotpath" contingency layer for multi-region GPU failover. The hotpath is a small, fast reserve pool designed to absorb short-term spikes and regional outages for latency-sensitive traffic (streaming/chat generation, low-latency inference). Goal: keep P95 latency SLA intact for 30 minutes during single-region impact while automated routing and scale-up occur.

Summary table (snapshot 2026-07-12):
Region, GPU_Type, Total_GPUs, Baseline_Util_pct, Target_Hotpath_pct, Hotpath_Gpus, Rotational_WarmPool_Gpus, Failover_Target_Region, Notes
us-west1, H100-80GB, 1280, 78, 4, 51, 12, us-east4, primary west coast demand spike, close to baseline
us-east4, H100-80GB, 1152, 81, 5, 58, 10, europe-west1, high baseline; slightly higher headroom target
europe-west1, A100-40GB, 720, 70, 6, 43, 8, us-east4, regional pricing allows warm capacity reuse
asia-south1, A100-40GB, 384, 62, 8, 31, 6, europe-west1, smaller pool; prefer cross-region warm ramps
canary-zone (us-central-temp), T4x2, 64, 40, 25, 16, 4, us-west1, cheap burst-capacity for canary/fallback

Key formulas (applied per-region):
- Hotpath_Gpus = ceil(total_gpus * Target_Hotpath_pct / 100)
- Rotational_WarmPool_Gpus = max(ceil(Hotpath_Gpus * 0.2), 4)  # floor of 4 to allow rotation and testing
- Failover_Capacity_Needed = sum(hotpath_gpus of impacted region) * regional_latency_factor

Assumptions and rationale:
- Hotpath is intentionally small (3-8% depending on region) and composed of highest-performance instances (H100 where available). Reason: latency SLOs are tight for streaming; cheaper GPUs increase token latency due to mixed precision and kernel variances.
- Rotational warm pool provides continuous testing of failover readiness: time-boxed weekly rotation of 15% of warm pool into active hotpath for 1 hour to validate correctness and KV cache priming.
- Failover targets chosen by network proximity and available spare H100 inventory. Preference ranking: same continent H100 -> same continent A100 -> cross-continent H100.

Risk scenarios modeled (short summary):
- Single rack failure (10-20% of region): hotpath absorbs within 2 minutes; rotational warm pool provides immediate replacement if hotpath saturates.
- Full AZ down (25-40%): hotpath + warm pool partially absorb for 30 minutes; automatic routing + cloud provider DR scale-in triggered by autoscaler.
- Full region outage (>60%): hotpath provides short runway but cross-region capacity must be pulled; expected P95 degradation during DNS failover window (~45-90s) mitigated by faster edge routing.

Operational runbook snippets (short):
- Triage step 0: detect region impact via per-region P95 and queue-length signals. Alert: region_p95 > sla_threshold OR inflight_queue > 10k tokens
- Step 1: Activate hotpath promotion policy: move latency-sensitive routes to local hotpath instances; route best-effort to secondary regions.
- Step 2: Trigger warm-pool rotation to fill any gaps and mark nodes as "in-play". Run KV cache priming for top-50 prompts in the last 24h.
- Step 3: Notify SRE on-call; start cross-region capacity allocation job (JIRA-OPS-7892) and enable prioritized preemption rules for dedicated capacity customers (if allowed by contract).
- Postmortem: record hit-rate on hotpath, fill-adjust targets for next 30 days if utilization > 70% for > 1 hour.

Monitoring metrics to add to Console (per-region and global):
- Hotpath_utilization_pct (hotpath_gpus_active / hotpath_gpus_total)
- WarmPool_rotation_success_pct (rotations without cache-miss regressions)
- Failover_absorb_time (seconds until baseline traffic re-stabilizes)
- Excess_latency_tokens (token-count weighted latency uplift during failover)

Capacity tuning knobs (to include in Optimize recommendations):
- Target_Hotpath_pct: 3-8%, can be tuned monthly based on historical surge frequency per region.
- Rotational cadence: weekly by default; increase to 3x/week for high-change regions.
- Prioritized preemption window: 10 minutes by default; shorten to 5 minutes during severe outages.

Cost impact estimate (rough, monthly):
- Global hotpath (across regions above): ~210 H100-equivalent GPUs => ~$1.2M/mo at list rates; expected internal negotiated discounts reduce by ~28%.
- Warm-pool churn (rotation + cache priming): adds ~6% egress and ephemeral startup GPU-hours; model expects ~0.7% increase in monthly bill.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Contract constraints: can we preempt Dedicated customers for <15m emergency absorb? (FYI: legal review ticket CONFLUENCE-Infra-Hotpath-2026 has notes)
- Can we standardize on H100 family for hotpath globally, or do we accept mixed H100/A100 hotpath composition in APAC?
- Should hotpath autoscaling be aggressive (scale by 50% within 3 minutes) or conservative (25% within 5 minutes) given startup cold cache penalties?

Next steps and owners:
- Implement per-region Hotpath_allocations in infra config (owner: Priya Natarajan) - JIRA-OPS-7892
- Console dashboard tiles for hotpath metrics (owner: Samir Patel) - add to sprint 42
- Run 3 scheduled warm-pool failover drills over next 60 days and capture metrics (owner: Jill Harper)

Notes to reviewers:
- This sheet is intentionally concise; more detailed cost modeling and simulator inputs exist in linked Confluence pages. Use this doc to get alignment on target %s and rotation policy before we convert into a formal runbook.

Quick diffs from prior capacity docs:
- Focus on a kept-small, high-performance "hotpath" rather than a large passive reserve. Emphasizes rotation/testing and KV cache priming to reduce cold-start penalties.
- Explicit operational checklist and metric set for SRE/Console visibility.

Scratchpad / raw numbers used for simulations (kept brief):
- 1 H100 = baseline throughput unit; A100 considered 0.75 H100 for hotpath math.
- Latency multiplier for cross-region failover = 1.35 (P95 expected uplift).
- Rotation success target = 98% (no user-facing impact during rotation).

End of worksheet.

Unresolved: confirm hotpath preemption policy with commercial (blocked: CONFLUENCE-Infra-Hotpath-2026).
